PNN-003 Alibi on a short leash

Two walks. One tight alibi.

Two Tightie Whities. Two dogs. A few minutes apart. PNN examines a routine walk that became considerably less routine when somebody asked a follow-up question.

Subject team
Tightie Whities
Opened
October 7, 2026 at 9:46 PM (America/Denver)
PNN threat rating
Suspiciously well exercised

The incident

An anonymous source out walking their dog reported encountering two different members of the Tightie Whities, each also walking a dog, heading downhill just a few minutes apart. One team member's dog ownership came as news to the witness. Asked how long they had owned the dog, the member appeared, in the witness's estimation, to struggle for an answer. A simple walk had acquired a surprisingly difficult history section. PNN notes that 'How long have you had your dog?' is not usually considered an advanced question.

Suspected motive

PNN theory: leave a secret team meeting in staggered departures, or scout a future prank under cover of canine exercise. A few minutes between teammates would look beautifully inconspicuous, provided nobody encountered both of them. Unfortunately, the neighborhood had assigned the same witness to both exits. An administrative setback for the alleged operation.

Investigator's note

Clueso's reconstruction gives the alleged plan three stages: bring a dog, leave separately, survive small talk. The first two appear manageable. The third may require another team meeting. He had hoped to find the Prowling Purrpetrators behind the whole affair; instead, the pink suspects remain uncaught while he opens a file on dog-walking logistics.

Official PNN assessment

The secret meeting remains a PNN theory. The prank-scouting theory also remains available, should the first theory need a walk. The Tightie Whities' alibi is now on a short leash. Next time, PNN recommends knowing the dog's backstory before taking it on a cover story.
